measured_or_observed_evidence.result: PR204 parent candidate reached physical Gate baseline and ClayCode contract but failed the same-execution second reservation; root cause is UNIQUE(binding_hash), which incorrectly enforces one effect per execution generation.

The temporary duplicate #204 schema patch in this run was therefore reverted to preserve branch ownership/topology.
Gate-issued identity is held in process-local WeakSet/WeakKeyDictionary structures; without process-incarnation validation these objects are candidates for fork inheritance.

hypothesis.statement: Exact-object Gate issuance plus V15/V16 identity is necessary but not sufficient on POSIX if a child process inherits the Gate lease object, process-local capability registries/secrets and flock open-file-description through fork. Effect authority must additionally be bound to the issuing OS process incarnation before copied registries/locks are consulted.

strongest_counterhypothesis.statement: Production Frank may never fork while an execution lease is live, making the inheritance path unreachable. This can reduce operational reachability but does not establish process-local copied state as a valid authority primitive; exact target #233 remains the discriminator.

external_primary_evidence.finding: flock locks are associated with an open file description; descriptors inherited via fork/dup refer to the same lock. flock is advisory on ordinary local Linux filesystems.
Python exposes child/parent fork hooks, but third-party C forks may bypass them unless the CPython fork hooks are called; therefore at-fork cleanup alone is not the strongest authority guard.

snapshot restore can move revisions backward; revision bump/compaction is recommended to prevent old revision assumptions and stale caches from remaining plausible. This supports a separate restore-incarnation layer beyond process incarnation.
